  $$t = \frac{300\text{ m}}{5\text{ m/s}} = 60\text{ seconds}$$

💡 Tip: River current flowing North does NOT slow down or speed up crossing East.

easy.question: In the scenario above (Width = 300 m, v_boat = 5 m/s East, v_river = 3 m/s North), how far downstream (North) is the boat pushed by the current upon reaching the opposite bank?
easy.explanation:
• Formula: $\text{Drift} = \text{River Speed} \times \text{Crossing Time}$
• Given: River speed $= 3\text{ m/s}$, Crossing time $= 60\text{ s}$
• Calculation:
  $$\text{Drift} = 3\text{ m/s} \times 60\text{ s} = 180\text{ meters (North)}$$

💡 Tip: The boat is pushed downstream while crossing.

easy.question: What is the resultant speed of the boat relative to a stationary observer on the riverbank during the Direct Dash?
easy.explanation:
• Formula: Resultant ground speed $= \sqrt{v_{\text{boat}}^2 + v_{\text{river}}^2}$
• Given: Boat speed East $= 5\text{ m/s}$, River speed North $= 3\text{ m/s}$
• Calculation:
  $$v_{\text{ground}} = \sqrt{5^2 + 3^2} = \sqrt{25 + 9} = \sqrt{34} \approx 5.83\text{ m/s}$$

💡 Tip: Use the Pythagorean theorem for perpendicular velocities.

easy.question: To cross a river along the shortest possible path (landing directly opposite the start with zero drift), the boat must be steered:

options.label: Upstream at an angle to the perpendicular
Downstream at an angle to the perpendicular

easy.explanation:
• Key Rule for Zero Drift (Straight Across):
  - The boat must steer upstream so its upstream speed cancels the river current:
    $$\sin\theta = \frac{v_{\text{river}}}{v_{\text{boat}}}$$
  - Since $\sin\theta$ cannot exceed 1, this is only possible if boat speed is **greater** than river speed ($v_{\text{boat}} > v_{\text{river}}$).

💡 Tip: You cannot land straight across if the river flows faster than you can swim.

easy.question: Two cars A and B travel along a straight highway in the same direction. Car A moves at 80 km/h and Car B moves at 60 km/h. What is the velocity of Car A relative to Car B?
easy.explanation:
• Formula: Relative Speed $= v_A - v_B$ (Same Direction)
• Given: Car A $= 80\text{ km/h}$, Car B $= 60\text{ km/h}$
• Calculation:
  $$v_{\text{rel}} = 80 - 60 = 20\text{ km/h (forward)}$$

💡 Tip: Moving in the same direction? Subtract speeds.

easy.question: Which of the following statements regarding 2D river-boat motion are TRUE?

options.label: The time to cross the river is minimized when the boat is steered directly across (θ = 0°)
The crossing time is completely independent of the river current speed when pointing directly across
The resultant velocity relative to ground is the vector sum v_boat/ground = v_boat/water + v_water/ground
Steering upstream reduces the effective eastward crossing speed

easy.explanation:
• Key River-Boat Principles:
  - Shortest time to cross: Aim straight across ($	heta = 0^circ$).
  - Shortest path (zero drift): Aim upstream ($sin	heta = v_r / v_b$).
  - Perpendicular velocity components are completely independent.

💡 Tip: All 4 statements are standard 2D relative motion rules.

easy.question: A person standing inside a train moving with uniform velocity throws an apple vertically upwards. Which statements are correct?

options.label: For the person inside the train, the path of the apple is a vertical straight line
For an observer on the ground, the path of the apple is a parabola
The apple falls back into the thrower's hand (assuming negligible air resistance)
The acceleration of the apple is different in both reference frames

easy.explanation:
• Reference Frames:
  - **Inside the train**: The thrower moves with the train, so they see the ball go **straight up and down**.
  - **From the ground**: The ball moves upward AND forward with the train, tracing a **parabola**.

💡 Tip: What looks straight inside a moving vehicle looks parabolic from the ground.

easy.question: Two trains of lengths 100 m and 150 m move on parallel tracks. Which statements are TRUE?

options.label: Total relative distance to completely cross each other is 250 m
Relative speed when moving in opposite directions is the sum of their individual speeds
Relative speed when moving in the same direction is the difference of their individual speeds
Crossing time is shorter when they travel in opposite directions

easy.explanation:
• Step-by-Step:
  1. Total distance for complete overtake = Sum of train lengths:
     $$d = 100\text{ m} + 150\text{ m} = 250\text{ m}$$
  2. Relative speed (same direction) = $25 - 15 = 10\text{ m/s}$.
  3. Time $= \frac{250\text{ m}}{10\text{ m/s}} = 25\text{ seconds}$.

💡 Tip: For extended bodies, add lengths to get the total overtake distance.

easy.question: Rain is falling vertically downwards at speed v_r. A person walks horizontally with speed v_m. Which of the following are TRUE?

options.label: Relative velocity of rain with respect to the person is v_rain/man = v_r - v_m
The person must hold the umbrella tilted forward in the direction of motion
The apparent speed of raindrops hitting the person is sqrt(v_r^2 + v_m^2)
The tilt angle with the vertical is tan(θ) = v_m / v_r

easy.explanation:
• Umbrella Tilt in Rain:
  - Relative velocity of rain to runner: $\vec{v}_{\text{rel}} = \vec{v}_{\text{rain}} - \vec{v}_{\text{runner}}$
  - Tilt angle with vertical: $\tan\theta = \frac{v_{\text{runner}}}{v_{\text{rain}}}$
  - Tilt umbrella forward to face the oncoming relative raindrops.

💡 Tip: Running faster makes rain hit your front at a steeper angle.

easy.question: When a swimmer crosses a flowing river:

options.label: Crossing time is minimum when swimming perpendicular to the river bank
In minimum time crossing, the drift downstream is always non-zero (if river speed > 0)
The actual path followed relative to the ground is along the resultant velocity vector
River flow increases the swimmer's speed relative to the water

easy.explanation:
• Key Concept:
  - A swimmer's speed relative to the water is determined by their own swimming effort.
  - River current changes the swimmer's path relative to the ground, but not their swimming speed in the water.

💡 Tip: The water carries you downstream, but your swimming speed through water remains the same.

easy.question: A fighter jet is flying at 100 m/s, chasing a tanker jet moving at 100 m/s 35 meters ahead. If the fighter speeds up to 105 m/s, how many seconds will it take to close the 35 m gap?
easy.explanation:
• Step-by-Step:
  1. Relative speed of approach $= 105 - 100 = 5\text{ m/s}$.
  2. Distance to close $= 200\text{ meters}$.
  3. Time $= \frac{200\text{ m}}{5\text{ m/s}} = 40\text{ seconds}$.

💡 Tip: Intercept time depends only on the speed difference ($5\text{ m/s}$).

easy.question: Two cars travel towards each other on a straight road at 20 m/s and 30 m/s. If they start 500 m apart, after how many seconds do they collide?
easy.explanation:
• Step-by-Step:
  1. Moving towards each other (opposite directions) $\implies$ add speeds:
     $$v_{\text{approach}} = 20 + 30 = 50\text{ m/s}$$
  2. Time $= \frac{\text{Distance}}{v_{\text{approach}}} = \frac{500\text{ m}}{50\text{ m/s}} = 10\text{ seconds}$.

💡 Tip: Head-on vehicles close distance at the sum of their speeds.

easy.question: A swimmer can swim at 4 m/s in still water. He crosses a 200 m wide river pointing directly across. The river flows at 3 m/s. What is the total time (in seconds) to reach the opposite bank?
easy.explanation:
• Calculation:
  $$\text{Time} = \frac{\text{Width}}{\text{Swimmer Speed Across}} = \frac{200\text{ m}}{4\text{ m/s}} = 50\text{ seconds}$$

💡 Tip: River current does not affect perpendicular crossing time.

easy.question: In the question above (Width = 200 m, v_swimmer = 4 m/s, v_river = 3 m/s), what is the magnitude of the swimmer's velocity relative to the ground (in m/s)?
easy.explanation:
• Calculation:
  $$v_{\text{ground}} = \sqrt{4^2 + 3^2} = \sqrt{16 + 9} = \sqrt{25} = 5\text{ m/s}$$

💡 Tip: $4\text{ m/s}$ across and $3\text{ m/s}$ downstream form a 3-4-5 right triangle.

easy.question: Two parallel trains of length 120 m and 80 m travel in opposite directions at 15 m/s and 10 m/s respectively. How many seconds does it take for them to completely pass each other?
easy.explanation:
• Step-by-Step:
  1. Total clearance distance $= 120 + 80 = 200\text{ m}$.
  2. Relative speed (opposite directions) $= 15 + 10 = 25\text{ m/s}$.
  3. Crossing time $= \frac{200\text{ m}}{25\text{ m/s}} = 8\text{ seconds}$.

💡 Tip: Add lengths and add speeds for opposite directions.

medium.question: A boat with speed 5 m/s in still water crosses a 300 m wide river flowing North at 3 m/s. What upstream angle θ (South of East) must the boat maintain to hit the escape pad directly across?
medium.explanation:
• Formula: $\sin\theta = \frac{v_{\text{river}}}{v_{\text{boat}}}$
• Given: River current $= 3\text{ m/s}$, Boat speed $= 5\text{ m/s}$
• Calculation:
  $$\sin\theta = \frac{3}{5} = 0.6 \implies \theta = \arcsin(0.6) \approx 36.87^\circ\text{ upstream}$$

💡 Tip: Steering upstream at $36.87^\circ$ cancels the river flow completely.

medium.question: What is the effective ground crossing speed vx of the boat during the Precision Landing (when steered at θ = 36.87° South of East)?
medium.explanation:
• Formula: Effective cross-river speed $v_x = \sqrt{v_{\text{boat}}^2 - v_{\text{river}}^2}$
• Calculation:
  $$v_x = \sqrt{5^2 - 3^2} = \sqrt{25 - 9} = \sqrt{16} = 4\text{ m/s}$$

💡 Tip: Part of the boat's speed is used to fight current, leaving $4\text{ m/s}$ forward speed.

medium.question: How long does the boat take to cross the 300 m river during the Precision Landing (0 drift)?
medium.explanation:
• Calculation:
  $$\text{Crossing Time} = \frac{\text{River Width}}{v_x} = \frac{300\text{ m}}{4\text{ m/s}} = 75\text{ seconds}$$

💡 Tip: Zero-drift crossing takes $75\text{ s}$ compared to $60\text{ s}$ for straight crossing.

medium.question: A man walks at 3 km/h and rain appears to fall vertically on him. When he increases his speed to 6 km/h, rain appears to hit him at 45° to the vertical. What is the true speed of the raindrops?
medium.explanation:
• Step-by-Step:
  1. At $3\text{ km/h}$, rain appears vertical $\implies$ rain's horizontal speed is $3\text{ km/h}$.
  2. At $6\text{ km/h}$, rain appears at $45^\circ$ $\implies$ vertical speed is $6 - 3 = 3\text{ km/h}$.
  3. True rain speed $= \sqrt{3^2 + 3^2} = \sqrt{18} = 3\sqrt{2}\text{ km/h}$.

💡 Tip: Two different walking speeds reveal both horizontal and vertical rain components.

medium.question: An airplane flies from city A to city B (due East, distance 1200 km) and back. Plane airspeed is 500 km/h and wind blows due East at 100 km/h. What is the total round-trip flight time?
medium.explanation:
• Step-by-Step:
  1. Outward (Tailwind): Speed $= 500 + 100 = 600\text{ km/h} \implies t_1 = \frac{1200}{600} = 2.0\text{ h}$.
  2. Return (Headwind): Speed $= 500 - 100 = 400\text{ km/h} \implies t_2 = \frac{1200}{400} = 3.0\text{ h}$.
  3. Total round-trip time $= 2.0 + 3.0 = 5.0\text{ hours}$.

💡 Tip: Wind increases total round-trip time because you spend more time in the slow headwind.

medium.question: A boat crosses a river of width W with speed v_b relative to water. The river flows with speed v_r (v_b > v_r). Which statements are TRUE?

options.label: The ratio of minimum time to time taken for shortest path is sqrt(1 - (v_r/v_b)^2)
The direction for minimum time is perpendicular to the river bank
The angle with upstream for shortest path is 90° + arcsin(v_r/v_b)
Shortest path crossing time is always strictly greater than minimum crossing time

medium.explanation:
• Ratio of Crossing Times:
  - Minimum time (straight across): $t_1 = \frac{W}{v_b}$
  - Shortest path (zero drift): $t_2 = \frac{W}{\sqrt{v_b^2 - v_r^2}}$
  - Ratio $\frac{t_1}{t_2} = \frac{\sqrt{v_b^2 - v_r^2}}{v_b}$

💡 Tip: Zero-drift crossing always takes longer because part of the velocity is directed upstream.

medium.question: A swimmer wishes to cross a river to reach the exact point directly opposite on the other bank. Which conditions allow this?

options.label: Swimmer's speed in still water must be strictly greater than the river flow speed
The swimmer must angle upstream at sin θ = v_river / v_swimmer
If river flow speed exceeds swimming speed, zero drift is impossible
The resultant velocity relative to ground will be perpendicular to the river banks

medium.explanation:
• Zero-Drift Swimmer Conditions:
  - Must steer upstream ($sin	heta = v_{\text{river}}/v_{\text{swimmer}}$).
  - Feasible only when swimmer speed exceeds river speed ($v_s > v_r$).
  - Effective crossing speed is $\sqrt{v_s^2 - v_r^2}$.
  - Ground path is straight across perpendicular to the bank.

💡 Tip: All 4 statements are essential rules for landing straight across.

medium.question: Two particles 1 and 2 move with constant velocities v1 and v2. Their initial position vectors are r1 and r2. For them to collide:

options.label: Their relative velocity vector (v1 - v2) must be directed along (r2 - r1)
Their relative acceleration must be non-zero
Time to collision is |r2 - r1| / |v1 - v2|

medium.explanation:
• Collision Condition for Two Moving Objects:
  - Position of Object 1: $\vec{r}_1 + \vec{v}_1 t$
  - Position of Object 2: $\vec{r}_2 + \vec{v}_2 t$
  - For collision: $\vec{r}_1 + \vec{v}_1 t = \vec{r}_2 + \vec{v}_2 t \implies \vec{r}_1 - \vec{r}_2 = (\vec{v}_2 - \vec{v}_1)t$
  - This means initial separation vector must align directly with relative velocity vector.

💡 Tip: For two moving objects to collide, their relative velocity must point straight along their separation line.

medium.question: An open rail car moves horizontally with uniform speed v0. Rain falls vertically with terminal velocity u. For an observer on the car:

options.label: Rain appears to fall at an angle θ = arctan(v0 / u) to the vertical
The apparent speed of rain is sqrt(v0^2 + u^2)
If the car accelerates horizontally with acceleration a, the apparent angle of rain changes with time
The vertical component of raindrop velocity changes due to car's horizontal motion

medium.explanation:
• Rail Car Moving in Rain:
  - Relative velocity of rain to rail car: $\vec{v}_{\text{rel}} = -v_0 \hat{i} - u \hat{j}$
  - Apparent tilt angle: $\tan\theta = v_0 / u$
  - Relative speed $= \sqrt{v_0^2 + u^2}$
  - Higher rail speed tilts the rain further back.

💡 Tip: All 4 statements are true for relative motion in rain.

medium.question: A helicopter at height H moves horizontally with speed u. It releases a supply crate toward a target. Which of the following statements are correct?

options.label: The crate inherits the horizontal velocity u of the helicopter at release
Time of fall is t = sqrt(2H / g)
Horizontal distance traveled by crate before hitting ground is u * sqrt(2H / g)
Relative to the pilot in uniform horizontal flight, the crate falls in a straight vertical line below the aircraft

medium.explanation:
• Bomb/Kit Dropped from Moving Helicopter:
  - Inside helicopter (pilot's frame): Kit drops **straight down** because horizontal speeds are equal.
  - From the ground: Kit follows a **parabolic path** combining horizontal forward motion and vertical gravity fall.

💡 Tip: Trajectory is straight vertical for the pilot, but a curved parabola for a ground observer.

medium.question: A 240 m wide river flows at 4 m/s. A boat travels at 5 m/s in still water. What is the minimum time (in seconds) required for the boat to cross the river?
medium.explanation:
• Minimum Time to Cross River:
  - Minimum time is achieved by aiming straight across ($90^\circ$ to bank).
  - Time $= \frac{\text{Width}}{\text{Boat Speed}} = \frac{240\text{ m}}{5\text{ m/s}} = 48\text{ seconds}$.

💡 Tip: To cross in the fastest time, always aim directly at the opposite bank.

medium.question: In the problem above (Width = 240 m, v_river = 4 m/s, v_boat = 5 m/s), what is the drift distance (in meters) when the boat crosses in minimum time?
medium.explanation:
• Downstream Drift Calculation:
  - Crossing time $= 48\text{ s}$
  - River pushes downstream at $4\text{ m/s}$
  - Drift $= 4\text{ m/s} \times 48\text{ s} = 192\text{ meters}$

💡 Tip: Drift distance = River current speed $\times$ crossing time.

medium.question: A helicopter flying horizontally at 40 m/s at an altitude of 125 m releases a package to hit a stationary boat on water. Taking g = 10 m/s², what horizontal distance (in meters) before the boat must the package be released?
medium.explanation:
• Step-by-Step:
  1. Fall time from height $125\text{ m}$:
     $$t = \sqrt{\frac{2H}{g}} = \sqrt{\frac{2 \times 125}{10}} = \sqrt{25} = 5\text{ seconds}$$
  2. Horizontal distance traveled by kit in $5\text{ s}$:
     $$x = 40\text{ m/s} \times 5\text{ s} = 200\text{ meters}$$

💡 Tip: The released kit flies forward $200\text{ m}$ before hitting the ground.

medium.question: A man standing on a road has to hold his umbrella at 30° with the vertical to keep rain off. He throws away the umbrella and starts running at 10 km/h; now rain hits him vertically. What is the speed of the rain relative to the ground (in km/h)?
medium.explanation:
• Step-by-Step:
  1. Rain falls at $30^\circ$ to vertical: $v_{r,x} = v_r \sin(30^\circ) = 0.5 v_r$.
  2. Man runs at $10\text{ km/h}$ and rain appears vertical $\implies$ man's speed matches rain's horizontal speed:
     $$0.5 v_r = 10\text{ km/h} \implies v_r = 20\text{ km/h}$$

💡 Tip: Matching the horizontal speed of rain makes it fall straight down relative to you.

medium.question: A river 400 m wide flows at 3 m/s. A motorboat whose speed in still water is 5 m/s crosses it along the shortest path (0 drift). How many seconds does the crossing take?
medium.explanation:
• Step-by-Step:
  1. Cross-river speed for zero drift:
     $$v_x = \sqrt{v_b^2 - v_r^2} = \sqrt{5^2 - 3^2} = 4\text{ m/s}$$
  2. Crossing time $= \frac{400\text{ m}}{4\text{ m/s}} = 100\text{ seconds}$.

💡 Tip: Zero-drift crossing time = $\frac{\text{Width}}{\sqrt{v_b^2 - v_r^2}}$.

advanced.question: If the river flow speed vr exceeds the boat speed vb (i.e. vr > vb), which of the following is TRUE regarding reaching the opposite bank?

options.label: The boat can still reach the directly opposite point if steered at θ = 90°
Zero drift is impossible; minimum drift occurs when sin θ = vb / vr
The boat cannot cross the river at all

advanced.explanation:
• Fast River Current ($v_r > v_b$):
  - When the river flows faster than the boat, zero drift is impossible.
  - To get the **minimum possible drift**, the boat must steer upstream at angle:
    $$\sin\theta = \frac{v_{\text{boat}}}{v_{\text{river}}}$$

💡 Tip: When river is faster than boat ($v_r > v_b$), minimum drift angle satisfies $\sin\theta = v_b / v_r$.

advanced.question: A helicopter flies at altitude H = 125 m with velocity v_h = 40î m/s. Directly below, a boat moves at v_boat = 15î m/s in the same direction. A payload is dropped (g = 10 m/s²). At what horizontal distance behind the boat must the payload be dropped to land on the boat?
advanced.explanation:
• Step-by-Step:
  1. Time to fall $125\text{ m}$: $t = \sqrt{2(125)/10} = 5\text{ s}$.
  2. Relative horizontal speed between helicopter ($30\text{ m/s}$) and boat ($10\text{ m/s}$):
     $$v_{\text{rel}} = 30 - 10 = 20\text{ m/s}$$
  3. Release distance behind the boat:
     $$D = 20\text{ m/s} \times 5\text{ s} = 100\text{ meters}$$

💡 Tip: Release $100\text{ m}$ early so the package overtakes and lands right on the boat.

advanced.question: A ship A steams due North at 20 km/h. Another ship B is 10 km due East of A and steams due West at 20 km/h. What is the shortest distance of closest approach between the two ships?
advanced.explanation:
• Closest Approach of Two Ships:
  - Ship A moves North at $20\text{ km/h}$; Ship B starts $10\text{ km}$ East and moves West at $20\text{ km/h}$.
  - Relative velocity forms a $45^\circ$ triangle with speed $20\sqrt{2}\text{ km/h}$.
  - Closest approach distance $= 10 \times \sin(45^\circ) = \frac{10}{\sqrt{2}} = 5\sqrt{2} \approx 7.07\text{ km}$.
  - Time to closest approach $= 15\text{ minutes}$.

💡 Tip: Closest approach distance = Initial separation $\times \sin(45^\circ)$.

advanced.question: Three particles A, B, and C are situated at the vertices of an equilateral triangle of side length L. Each particle moves with constant speed v toward the next particle in clockwise order (A towards B, B towards C, C towards A). How long do they take to meet at the centroid?
advanced.explanation:
• 3 Particles on an Equilateral Triangle (Side $L$, Speed $v$):
  - Each particle moves towards the next at angle $60^\circ$.
  - Rate of closing distance $= v + v \cos(60^\circ) = v(1 + 0.5) = 1.5v$.
  - Meeting time $= \frac{L}{1.5v} = \frac{2L}{3v}$.

💡 Tip: They spiral into the center and meet in time $\frac{2L}{3v}$.

advanced.question: Four particles A, B, C, D are at the four corners of a square of side d. Each particle moves with speed v aiming continuously at the next particle in cyclic order. The time when they collide at the center is:
advanced.explanation:
• 4 Particles on a Square (Side $L$, Speed $v$):
  - Adjacent velocities are perpendicular ($90^\circ$), so the closing speed is simply $v$.
  - Meeting time $= \frac{\text{Side Length}}{\text{Speed}} = \frac{L}{v}$.

💡 Tip: 4 chasing particles on a square meet at the center in time $L/v$.

advanced.question: In 2D relative motion between two particles with initial positions r1, r2 and constant velocities v1, v2:

options.label: The distance of closest approach is |(r1 - r2) × (v1 - v2)| / |v1 - v2|
The time of closest approach is -[(r1 - r2) • (v1 - v2)] / |v1 - v2|^2
If the distance of closest approach is 0, they collide at time t > 0
The trajectory of one particle viewed from the other is always a straight line

advanced.explanation: Relative position r_rel(t) = r_rel(0) + v_rel·t. Differentiating |r_rel(t)|² gives time of closest approach t = -(r0 • v_rel)/|v_rel|². The perpendicular distance from origin to line of relative motion is |r0 × v_rel|/|v_rel|. Since relative acceleration is 0, relative trajectory is a straight line.

advanced.question: A river flows with speed u. A swimmer can swim at speed v relative to water. If u > v:

options.label: The swimmer cannot cross to the directly opposite point on the opposite bank
Minimum drift occurs when swimming at an angle sin θ = v / u upstream
Minimum drift distance is W * sqrt(u^2 - v^2) / v
Minimum crossing time is still W / v, achieved at θ = 0°

advanced.explanation: When u > v, the current always overpowers perpendicular heading. Setting d(drift)/dθ = 0 yields sin θ = v/u. The minimum drift evaluates to W √(u² - v²) / v. Minimum time is always achieved at θ=0° with t = W/v.

advanced.question: A helicopter drops a rescue kit to a moving boat with a crosswind present (v_payload = v_heli + v_wind). Which of the following equations correctly govern interception?

options.label: Flight time is dictated purely by vertical fall: t_f = sqrt(2H / g)
Required initial x-offset is Δx = (v_heli_x + v_wind_x - v_boat_x) * t_f
Required initial y-offset is Δy = (v_heli_y + v_wind_y - v_boat_y) * t_f
Air drag along horizontal axes reduces effective relative travel distance

advanced.explanation: Vertical motion decouples completely under gravity giving t_f = √(2H/g). In 2D/3D, relative displacement equals relative velocity times time of flight for each independent axis. Air resistance decelerates horizontal momentum.

advanced.question: Two cars A and B move along intersecting straight roads at constant speeds v_A and v_B at an angle α to each other. Which statements are correct?

options.label: Magnitude of relative velocity is sqrt(v_A^2 + v_B^2 - 2 v_A v_B cos α)
The relative motion of B as observed from A is along a straight line
The rate of change of distance between them is equal to the magnitude of relative velocity only when moving directly along line of sight
Distance between them is minimum when relative position is perpendicular to relative velocity

advanced.explanation: Vector subtraction gives |v_rel| = √(v_A² + v_B² - 2v_A v_B cos α). Constant velocities guarantee straight-line relative trajectories. Rate of change of distance d(r)/dt = v_rel • r_hat (line-of-sight component), which equals |v_rel| only if purely radial. Minimum distance occurs when r_rel ⊥ v_rel.

advanced.question: A gun is mounted on a vehicle moving with velocity v_c. A shell is fired with muzzle velocity v_m relative to the barrel at angle θ to the horizontal in the forward direction. Which statements are TRUE?

options.label: Horizontal velocity of the shell relative to ground is v_c + v_m cos θ
Vertical velocity of the shell relative to ground is v_m sin θ
Time of flight is 2 v_m sin θ / g
Range on horizontal ground is (v_c + v_m cos θ) * (2 v_m sin θ / g)

advanced.explanation: By Galilean vector addition: v_ground = (v_c + v_m cos θ)î + (v_m sin θ)ĵ. Time of flight depends only on vertical component: T = 2uy/g = 2(v_m sin θ)/g. Ground range R = ux · T = (v_c + v_m cos θ) · T.

advanced.question: A river is 300 m wide and flows at 5 m/s. A boat has a speed of 3 m/s in still water. What is the minimum possible downstream drift (in meters) the boat can achieve while crossing?
advanced.explanation: Since vr (5) > vb (3), minimum drift occurs at sin θ = vb / vr = 3/5. Minimum drift = Width × √(vr² - vb²) / vb = 300 × √(25 - 9) / 3 = 300 × (4 / 3) = 400 meters.

advanced.question: A drone patrols along the riverbank at 10 m/s North. A boat starts from the opposite bank (300 m away) with v_boat = 5 m/s East and river flow v_river = 3 m/s North. If the drone starts 600 m South of the boat's initial East-projection line, how far from the boat (in meters) is the drone at the instant the boat hits the opposite bank?
advanced.explanation: Boat crossing time t = 300 / 5 = 60 s. Boat y-coordinate at finish = 3 × 60 = +180 m. Drone position after 60 s: y_D = -600 + (10 × 60) = 0 m. Distance between them on the bank = |180 - 0| = 180 meters.

advanced.question: Two cars A and B start simultaneously from the same point. Car A moves North at 30 km/h and Car B moves East at 40 km/h. What is the rate at which distance between them is increasing (in km/h)?
advanced.explanation: Position of A: r_A = 30t ĵ. Position of B: r_B = 40t î. Separation distance r = √((40t)² + (30t)²) = √(1600t² + 900t²) = √(2500t²) = 50t. Rate of change of distance dr/dt = 50 km/h.

advanced.question: A river of width 200√3 m (approx 346.4 m) flows at 4 m/s. A boat travels at 2 m/s in still water. If the boat steers upstream to achieve minimum drift, how many seconds does it take to reach the opposite bank?

advanced.question: A person running at 6 m/s horizontally observes raindrops striking them vertically with a speed of 8 m/s. What is the true speed of the raindrops (in m/s) relative to the ground?

## Easy Tier: Operation Storm Shield (Rain-Man Vector Tilt)

Have you ever noticed that when you walk in the rain, raindrops seem to fall straight down, but the moment you start sprinting, they slam straight into your face? In physics, this happens because your forward running motion adds directly to the relative motion of the raindrops.

### 🎯 What is Asked in this Challenge?

You are controlling a runner sprinting through a heavy downpour ($v_{\text{rain}} = 6.0\text{ m/s}$) with varying wind conditions. You must calculate and set the exact forward tilt angle ($\theta$) of your umbrella so that its protective canopy aligns perfectly with the oncoming rain vector, keeping you completely dry ($0\%$ wetness) as you reach the shelter.

### Step-by-Step Kinematic Derivation

1. **Relative Velocity Vector:** The velocity of rain relative to the runner is the vector difference between the rain's velocity and the runner's velocity:
   `v_rel = v_rain - v_runner = (v_wind - v_runner)î - v_rain ĵ`
2. **Calculating Umbrella Tilt:** To deflect the rain, the umbrella must point directly opposite the oncoming relative rain stream. The angle $\theta$ from the vertical is:
   `tan(θ) = |v_wind - v_runner| / v_rain`
   `θ = arctan(|v_wind - v_runner| / v_rain)`
3. **Apparent Rain Speed:** The speed at which raindrops strike the umbrella is the Pythagorean hypotenuse:
   `v_apparent = √((v_wind - v_runner)² + v_rain²)`

### Key Insights & Pro-Tips

- **Zero Wind Case:** If wind is calm ($v_{\text{wind}} = 0$) and you run forward at $8\text{ m/s}$ with rain falling at $6\text{ m/s}$, $\tan\theta = 8/6 = 4/3 \approx 1.333 \implies \theta \approx 53.13^\circ$ tilted forward.
- **Tailwind Case:** A forward wind blows raindrops in the direction you are running, reducing your relative horizontal speed and decreasing the required tilt angle.
- **Headwind Case:** A headwind blows rain toward you, increasing the relative horizontal speed and requiring a steeper forward tilt!

---

## Medium Tier: Crosswind River Crossing & Escape Artist (2D Vector Navigation)

Navigating a vessel across water or flying an aircraft through crosswinds requires continuous vector compensation. If a river flows East and you steer straight North, your boat will be pushed Eastward into a diagonal ground path.

### 🎯 What is Asked in this Challenge?

You are piloting a high-speed craft across a river with current speed $v_r = 3\text{ m/s}$. To reach a designated extraction pad directly across without drifting into enemy patrol sectors, you must compute the upstream heading angle and navigate with precision.

### Step-by-Step Kinematic Derivation

1. **Vector Decomposition:** The ground velocity $\vec{v}_g$ is the vector sum of boat engine velocity $\vec{v}_b$ and river current $\vec{v}_r$.
2. **Zero Drift Condition:** To travel straight perpendicular to the banks, the upstream component of boat velocity must perfectly cancel the river current:
   `v_b * sin(θ) = v_r ⟹ sin(θ) = v_r / v_b`
3. **Effective Forward Speed:** The net speed directly across the river is:
   `v_crossing = √(v_b² - v_r²)`

---

## Advanced Tier: Crosswind Crab Landing (Aeroplane-Wind Vector Triangle)

Flying an aircraft through crosswinds requires precise vector triangle compensation. An aircraft's velocity relative to the ground is the vector sum of its true airspeed through the air mass and the wind velocity vector: `v_ground = v_plane + v_wind`.

### 🎯 What is Asked in this Challenge?

You are piloting a jet on final approach to runway 09L during severe crosswinds ($v_{\text{wind}} = 14\text{ to }22\text{ m/s}$). You must compute and apply the exact crab heading angle ($\theta = \arcsin(v_{\text{cross}} / v_{\text{air}})$) and throttle your airspeed so that the resultant ground track vector $\vec{v}_{\text{ground}}$ aligns strictly with the runway centerline for a zero-drift touchdown.

### Step-by-Step Kinematic Derivation

1. **Vector Addition in Moving Air Mass:**
   `v_ground = v_air + v_wind`
2. **Decomposing into Runway Coordinates (X = Lateral, Y = Along Runway):**
   `v_ground_x = v_air · sin(θ) + v_wind_x`
   `v_ground_y = v_air · cos(θ) + v_wind_y`
3. **Zero Cross-Track Drift Condition ($v_{\text{ground},x} = 0$):**
   `v_air · sin(θ) + v_wind_x = 0 ⟹ sin(θ) = -v_wind_x / v_air`
   `θ = arcsin(-v_wind_x / v_air)`
theory.fullConcept:
# 2D/3D Relative Kinematics, Vector Calculus & Rain-Man Mechanics

## 1. Galilean Vector Transformation in Moving Frames

For any two objects $A$ and $B$ moving in an inertial ground frame $G$, the position, velocity, and acceleration transformations are governed by linear Galilean relativity:
$$\vec{r}_{A/B} = \vec{r}_A - \vec{r}_B$$
$$\vec{v}_{A/B} = \vec{v}_A - \vec{v}_B$$
$$\vec{a}_{A/B} = \vec{a}_A - \vec{a}_B$$

When $\vec{a}_A = \vec{a}_B = \vec{g}$ (such as two projectiles in free fall), the relative acceleration is strictly zero ($\vec{a}_{A/B} = \vec{0}$), meaning the relative velocity $\vec{v}_{A/B}$ is constant and the relative trajectory is a straight line.

---

## 2. Mathematical Formalism of the Rain-Man Problem

Let the ground reference frame have unit vectors $\hat{i}$ (horizontal forward) and $\hat{j}$ (vertical upward).

1. **Ground Velocity of Rain:**
   $$\vec{v}_R = v_w\hat{i} - u\hat{j}$$
   where $v_w$ is horizontal wind velocity and $u = |v_{\text{rain}}|$ is vertical terminal raindrop velocity.

2. **Ground Velocity of Observer (Man):**
   $$\vec{v}_M = v_m\hat{i}$$

3. **Relative Velocity Vector:**
   $$\vec{v}_{R/M} = \vec{v}_R - \vec{v}_M = (v_w - v_m)\hat{i} - u\hat{j}$$

4. **Apparent Angle with the Vertical:**
   $$\tan\theta = \frac{|\vec{v}_{R/M} \cdot \hat{i}|}{|\vec{v}_{R/M} \cdot \hat{j}|} = \frac{|v_w - v_m|}{u}$$
   $$\theta = \arctan\left(\frac{|v_w - v_m|}{u}\right)$$

5. **Raindrop Flux & Shielding Condition:**
   The volumetric flux of raindrops striking the observer is proportional to the relative speed $|\vec{v}_{R/M}| = \sqrt{(v_w - v_m)^2 + u^2}$. An umbrella with unit normal $\hat{n}$ achieves optimal shielding when $\hat{n}$ is anti-parallel to $\vec{v}_{R/M}$:
   $$\hat{n}_{\text{umbrella}} = -\frac{\vec{v}_{R/M}}{|\vec{v}_{R/M}|}$$

---

## 3. River Crossing: Minimum Time vs. Shortest Path Optimization

For a river of width $W$ flowing with velocity $\vec{v}_r = v_r\hat{i}$, and a craft with speed $v_b$ relative to the water steered at angle $\theta$ upstream from the normal ($\hat{j}$):
$$\vec{v}_b = (-v_b\sin\theta)\hat{i} + (v_b\cos\theta)\hat{j}$$
$$\vec{v}_g = (v_r - v_b\sin\theta)\hat{i} + (v_b\cos\theta)\hat{j}$$

- **Case A: Shortest Path ($v_b > v_r$):**
  Set drift component to zero: $v_r - v_b\sin\theta = 0 \implies \sin\theta = v_r / v_b$.
  Crossing time: $t = \frac{W}{v_b\cos\theta} = \frac{W}{\sqrt{v_b^2 - v_r^2}}$.

- **Case B: Minimum Drift ($v_r > v_b$):**
  Drift $x(\theta) = (v_r - v_b\sin\theta) \cdot \frac{W}{v_b\cos\theta} = \frac{W}{v_b}(v_r\sec\theta - v_b\tan\theta)$.
  Setting $\frac{dx}{d\theta} = 0 \implies v_r\sec\theta\tan\theta - v_b\sec^2\theta = 0 \implies \sin\theta = \frac{v_b}{v_r}$.
  Minimum Drift: $x_{\min} = W\frac{\sqrt{v_r^2 - v_b^2}}{v_b}$.

---

## 4. Aeroplane-Wind Vector Triangle & Crosswind Crab Angle

For an aircraft maintaining airspeed $v_a$ through wind velocity $\vec{v}_w$:
$$\vec{v}_g = \vec{v}_a + \vec{v}_w$$
To eliminate cross-track error along a runway heading, the crab angle $\theta$ is given by:
$$\sin\theta = \frac{v_{w,\text{cross}}}{v_a}$$

easy.question: Rain is falling vertically downwards at 3 m/s. A man runs horizontally at 4 m/s. What is the speed of the rain relative to the man?
easy.explanation:
📌 Core Concept: Relative Velocity Vector in 2D: $\vec{v}_{\text{rel}} = \vec{v}_{\text{rain}} - \vec{v}_{\text{man}}$.

🔢 Step-by-Step Derivation:
1. Set Up Vector Coordinates: Let horizontal motion be $\hat{i}$ and downward motion be $-\hat{j}$.
2. Express Velocities: Velocity of Rain $\vec{v}_r = -3\hat{j}\text{ m/s}$. Velocity of Man $\vec{v}_m = +4\hat{i}\text{ m/s}$.
3. Compute Relative Velocity: $\vec{v}_{r/m} = \vec{v}_r - \vec{v}_m = -4\hat{i} - 3\hat{j}\text{ m/s}$.
4. Calculate Speed (Magnitude): $|\vec{v}_{r/m}| = \sqrt{(-4)^2 + (-3)^2} = \sqrt{16 + 9} = \sqrt{25} = 5\text{ m/s}$.

💡 First-Principles Intuition: Even though rain is falling at $3\text{ m/s}$, the runner's horizontal sprint at $4\text{ m/s}$ causes raindrops to slam into their front at an apparent combined speed of $5\text{ m/s}$ (3-4-5 right triangle).

easy.question: In the scenario above (rain falling vertically at 3 m/s, man running at 4 m/s), at what angle to the vertical must the man hold his umbrella to stay dry?
easy.explanation:
📌 Core Concept: Umbrella Shielding Angle: $\tan\theta = \frac{|v_{\text{horizontal}}|}{|v_{\text{vertical}}|}$.

🔢 Step-by-Step Derivation:
1. The umbrella canopy must align with the oncoming relative velocity vector $\vec{v}_{r/m} = -4\hat{i} - 3\hat{j}$.
2. The angle $\theta$ measured from the vertical (y-axis) satisfies: $\tan\theta = \frac{|v_x|}{|v_y|} = \frac{4\text{ m/s}}{3\text{ m/s}} = \frac{4}{3} \approx 1.333$.
3. Taking the inverse tangent: $\theta = \arctan(4/3) \approx 53.13^\circ$ tilted forward.

💡 Why Option A is a Common Trap: $\arctan(3/4) = 36.87^\circ$ is the angle with the **horizontal** (ground), but umbrella tilt is always measured from the **vertical** line!

easy.question: A river 12 m wide flows at 4 m/s. A boat is steered directly across (perpendicular to current) at 3 m/s relative to the water. How far downstream does the boat drift upon reaching the other side?
easy.explanation:
📌 Core Concept: Independence of Perpendicular Motions ($x$ and $y$).

🔢 Step-by-Step Solution:
1. Find Crossing Time: The river current acts purely downstream (along $x$) and has ZERO effect on crossing speed (along $y$). Crossing time $t = \frac{\text{River Width}}{v_{\text{boat},y}} = \frac{12\text{ m}}{3\text{ m/s}} = 4\text{ seconds}$.
2. Calculate Downstream Drift: During these 4 seconds, the river current pushes the boat horizontally at $4\text{ m/s}$: $\text{Drift } x = v_{\text{river}} \times t = 4\text{ m/s} \times 4\text{ s} = 16\text{ meters}$.

💡 Physical Intuition: Perpendicular velocities are independent. You can calculate crossing duration purely from the perpendicular speed, then find drift by multiplying with river flow speed.

easy.question: Two vectors A and B have magnitudes of 6 units and 8 units respectively and are perpendicular to each other. What is the magnitude of their resultant vector (A + B)?
easy.explanation:
📌 Core Concept: Vector Addition Formula: $|\vec{A} + \vec{B}| = \sqrt{A^2 + B^2 + 2AB\cos\theta}$.

🔢 Step-by-Step Solution:
1. Since vectors are orthogonal (perpendicular), $\theta = 90^\circ$ and $\cos 90^\circ = 0$.
2. The cross term vanishes: $|\vec{R}| = \sqrt{A^2 + B^2} = \sqrt{6^2 + 8^2} = \sqrt{36 + 64} = \sqrt{100} = 10\text{ units}$.

💡 Geometric Insight: Two perpendicular vectors form the two legs of a right-angled triangle. The resultant vector is simply the hypotenuse ($6^2 + 8^2 = 10^2$ Pythagorean triple).

easy.question: A person walks 30 m East, then 40 m North. What is the magnitude of the net displacement vector?
easy.explanation: Displacement vector Δr = 30î + 40ĵ m. Magnitude |Δr| = √(30² + 40²) = √(900 + 1600) = √2500 = 50 meters.

easy.question: If a person walking in rain increases their running speed, which of the following quantities CHANGE?

options.label: Absolute velocity of the rain relative to ground
Relative velocity of the rain with respect to the person
Umbrella tilt angle required to stay dry
Rate of raindrops striking the front of the person

easy.explanation:
📌 Core Concept: Observer Frame Transformations in Rain-Man Kinematics ($\vec{v}_{r/m} = \vec{v}_r - \vec{v}_m$).

🎯 Option-by-Option Breakdown:
• Option A (Absolute rain velocity) [INCORRECT]: The rain's true velocity relative to ground is determined by clouds and wind; the observer's sprint has no physical impact on the rain's actual descent in the Earth frame.
• Option B (Relative velocity of rain) [CORRECT]: $\vec{v}_{r/m} = \vec{v}_r - \vec{v}_m$. As horizontal running speed $v_m$ increases, the relative vector magnitude and direction change directly.
• Option C (Umbrella tilt angle) [CORRECT]: The optimal umbrella angle satisfies $\tan\theta = \frac{v_m}{v_{\text{rain}}}$. Higher running speed requires a steeper forward umbrella tilt.
• Option D (Rate of raindrops striking front) [CORRECT]: Higher relative speed increases the volumetric flux of rain intercepted per second through the frontal cross-sectional area.

💡 Physical Intuition: Standing still, rain falls on your head. Running fast makes the rain feel like horizontal missiles hitting your chest, requiring a forward-angled umbrella.

easy.question: Which of the following statements regarding vector addition and subtraction are TRUE?

options.label: |A + B| can be equal to |A - B| if vectors A and B are orthogonal
The maximum possible magnitude of (A + B) is |A| + |B|
The minimum possible magnitude of (A + B) is ||A| - |B||
A + B is always greater in magnitude than A - B

easy.explanation:
📌 Core Concept: Vector Parallelogram Law & Triangle Inequality: $|\vec{A} \pm \vec{B}| = \sqrt{A^2 + B^2 \pm 2AB\cos\theta}$.

🎯 Option-by-Option Breakdown:
• Option A ($|A+B| = |A-B|$ when orthogonal) [CORRECT]: When $\vec{A} \perp \vec{B}$, $\cos 90^\circ = 0$, so $|\vec{A} + \vec{B}| = |\vec{A} - \vec{B}| = \sqrt{A^2 + B^2}$.
• Option B (Maximum magnitude is $|A| + |B|$) [CORRECT]: When vectors are collinear and parallel ($\theta = 0^\circ$), $\cos 0^\circ = 1$, yielding the absolute upper bound $|A| + |B|$.
• Option C (Minimum magnitude is $||A| - |B||$) [CORRECT]: When vectors are anti-parallel ($\theta = 180^\circ$), $\cos 180^\circ = -1$, yielding the lower bound $||A| - |B||$.
• Option D ($A + B$ always greater than $A - B$) [INCORRECT]: For obtuse angles ($\theta > 90^\circ$), $\cos\theta < 0$, making $|\vec{A} - \vec{B}| > |\vec{A} + \vec{B}|$.

💡 Geometric Insight: Think of two vectors forming the diagonals of a parallelogram. The diagonals have equal length if and only if the parallelogram is a rectangle (orthogonal vectors).

easy.question: A boat crosses a river of width W flowing with speed v_r. The boat speed in still water is v_b. When the boat heads directly perpendicular to the current (θ = 0°):

options.label: Crossing time is independent of river speed v_r
Drift along the bank is W * (v_r / v_b)
Net distance traveled relative to ground is W * sqrt(1 + (v_r/v_b)^2)

easy.explanation:
📌 Core Concept: Perpendicular Independence in 2D River Navigation.

🎯 Option-by-Option Breakdown:
• Option A ($t = W / v_b$) [CORRECT]: The across-river velocity is purely $v_b$. Crossing time is $t = \frac{W}{v_b}$ (shortest possible crossing time).
• Option B (Independent of river speed $v_r$) [CORRECT]: River flow acts entirely along the bank ($x$-axis) and cannot speed up or slow down crossing along the $y$-axis.
• Option C (Drift is $W \cdot \frac{v_r}{v_b}$) [CORRECT]: Downstream drift is $x = v_r \times t = v_r \left(\frac{W}{v_b}\right) = W\frac{v_r}{v_b}$.
• Option D (Net ground distance $W\sqrt{1 + (v_r/v_b)^2}$) [CORRECT]: Net ground displacement is $s = \sqrt{W^2 + x^2} = \sqrt{W^2 + W^2(v_r/v_b)^2} = W\sqrt{1 + (v_r/v_b)^2}$.

💡 Key Insight: Steering straight across ($90^\circ$ to bank) minimizes crossing duration, but creates downstream drift.

easy.question: Rain falls vertically at speed v_r. A cyclist rides with velocity v_c. Which statements are correct?

options.label: To an observer standing on the ground, raindrops fall along vertical lines
To the moving cyclist, raindrops appear to fall inclined backwards towards them
The apparent speed of rain increases with cyclist speed
If the cyclist reverses direction at same speed, the magnitude of relative rain speed remains identical

easy.explanation:
📌 Core Concept: Relative Velocity in Moving Frames ($\vec{v}_{r/c} = -v_c\hat{i} - v_r\hat{j}$).

🎯 Option-by-Option Breakdown:
• Option A (Vertical in ground frame) [CORRECT]: In the stationary ground frame, raindrops fall straight down with $\vec{v}_r = -v_r\hat{j}$.
• Option B (Inclined towards moving cyclist) [CORRECT]: In the cyclist's moving frame, the rain acquires an apparent backward horizontal component ($-v_c\hat{i}$), striking from the front.
• Option C (Apparent speed increases with cyclist speed) [CORRECT]: Relative speed is $v_{\text{apparent}} = \sqrt{v_r^2 + v_c^2}$, which monotonically grows as $v_c$ increases.
• Option D (Identical relative speed upon reversing) [CORRECT]: Reversing direction changes $\vec{v}_c \to -\vec{v}_c$, but $(-v_c)^2 = v_c^2$, so magnitude $\sqrt{v_r^2 + v_c^2}$ remains strictly equal.

💡 Physical Intuition: Whether cycling East or West at $10\text{ m/s}$, the rain feels equally fast, but comes from the opposite facing direction.

easy.question: Consider two vectors A = 3î + 4ĵ and B = 4î - 3ĵ. Which of the following are TRUE?

options.label: The dot product A • B is 0
Vectors A and B are perpendicular to each other
Both vectors have equal magnitudes of 5 units
The magnitude of vector (A + B) is 5√2

easy.explanation:
📌 Core Concept: Dot Product & Orthogonal Vector Properties ($\vec{A} \cdot \vec{B} = A_x B_x + A_y B_y$).

🎯 Option-by-Option Breakdown:
• Option A (Dot product is 0) [CORRECT]: $\vec{A} \cdot \vec{B} = (3)(4) + (4)(-3) = 12 - 12 = 0$.
• Option B (Perpendicular) [CORRECT]: A zero scalar product ($\vec{A} \cdot \vec{B} = 0$) for non-zero vectors guarantees that $\vec{A} \perp \vec{B}$ (angle $\theta = 90^\circ$).
• Option C (Equal magnitudes of 5 units) [CORRECT]: $|\vec{A}| = \sqrt{3^2 + 4^2} = 5$ and $|\vec{B}| = \sqrt{4^2 + (-3)^2} = 5$.
• Option D (Magnitude of $A + B$ is $5\sqrt{2}$) [CORRECT]: Resultant $\vec{A} + \vec{B} = (3+4)\hat{i} + (4-3)\hat{j} = 7\hat{i} + 1\hat{j}$. Magnitude $|\vec{A}+\vec{B}| = \sqrt{7^2 + 1^2} = \sqrt{50} = 5\sqrt{2}$.

💡 Geometric Insight: Two perpendicular vectors of equal length $L=5$ form a square, whose diagonal resultant is always $L\sqrt{2} = 5\sqrt{2}$.

easy.question: Rain is falling vertically at 6 m/s. A girl walks at 8 m/s. What is the apparent speed of the raindrops as felt by the girl (in m/s)?
easy.explanation:
📌 Core Concept: Relative Velocity Magnitude: $v_{\text{rel}} = \sqrt{v_{\text{rain}}^2 + v_{\text{walk}}^2}$.

🔢 Step-by-Step Solution:
1. Given: Vertical rain speed $v_{\text{rain}} = 6\text{ m/s}$, Horizontal walking speed $v_{\text{walk}} = 8\text{ m/s}$.
2. Pythagorean Resolution: $v_{\text{rel}} = \sqrt{6^2 + 8^2} = \sqrt{36 + 64} = \sqrt{100} = 10\text{ m/s}$.

💡 Physical Intuition: The girl's forward motion adds an apparent $8\text{ m/s}$ headwind component to the $6\text{ m/s}$ downward rain, creating a resultant $10\text{ m/s}$ velocity vector.

easy.question: A boat crosses a 180 m wide river flowing at 2 m/s. The boat is steered directly across at 3 m/s in still water. How many seconds does it take to cross?
easy.explanation:
📌 Core Concept: Independent Crossing Time: $t = \frac{\text{River Width}}{v_{\text{boat}}}$.

🔢 Step-by-Step Solution:
1. Given: Width $W = 180\text{ m}$, Across-river speed $v_{\text{boat}} = 3\text{ m/s}$.
2. Calculate Time: $t = \frac{180\text{ m}}{3\text{ m/s}} = 60\text{ seconds}$.

💡 Important Rule: River flow does NOT change the crossing time when steered directly across.

easy.question: In the question above (Width = 180 m, v_river = 2 m/s, v_boat = 3 m/s), what is the total downstream drift distance (in meters)?
easy.explanation:
📌 Core Concept: Downstream Drift Displacement: $x = v_{\text{river}} \times t$.

🔢 Step-by-Step Solution:
1. Given: River speed $v_{\text{river}} = 2\text{ m/s}$, Crossing time $t = 60\text{ s}$.
2. Calculate Drift: $x = 2\text{ m/s} \times 60\text{ s} = 120\text{ meters}$.

💡 Physical Intuition: The boat travels forward across the river for 60 seconds while simultaneously being swept downstream by 2 meters every second.

easy.question: A vector has an x-component of 12 units and a y-component of 5 units. What is its total magnitude?
easy.explanation:
📌 Core Concept: Vector Magnitude from Orthogonal Components: $|\vec{V}| = \sqrt{V_x^2 + V_y^2}$.

🔢 Step-by-Step Solution:
1. Given: $V_x = 12\text{ units}$, $V_y = 5\text{ units}$.
2. Compute Magnitude: $|\vec{V}| = \sqrt{12^2 + 5^2} = \sqrt{144 + 25} = \sqrt{169} = 13\text{ units}$.

💡 Geometric Insight: $5, 12, 13$ is a standard Pythagorean triple ($5^2 + 12^2 = 13^2$).

easy.question: A swimmer can swim at 5 m/s in still water. A river flows at 3 m/s. What is the swimmer's maximum possible speed relative to ground when swimming directly downstream (in m/s)?
easy.explanation: Downstream speed = v_swimmer + v_river = 5 + 3 = 8 m/s.

medium.question: A boat crosses a river of width W in minimum time t1. It crosses the same river along the shortest path (zero drift) in time t2. If river speed is u and boat speed in still water is v (v > u), the ratio t1 / t2 is:
medium.explanation: Minimum time t1 = W / v (steered directly across at θ = 0°). Shortest path requires zero drift, so effective crossing speed is √(v² - u²), giving t2 = W / √(v² - u²). Ratio t1 / t2 = (W/v) / (W/√(v² - u²)) = √(v² - u²) / v.

medium.question: Wind is blowing from North to South at 20 m/s. A pilot wishes to fly a plane due East. If the plane's airspeed in still air is 40 m/s, at what angle North of East must the pilot head the aircraft?
medium.explanation: To cancel the southward wind of 20 m/s, the plane must have a northward velocity component equal to 20 m/s: v_plane sin θ = v_wind ⟹ 40 sin θ = 20 ⟹ sin θ = 0.5 ⟹ θ = 30° North of East.

medium.question: In the navigation problem above (airspeed 40 m/s, wind 20 m/s South, heading 30° North of East), what is the resulting ground speed of the airplane towards East?
medium.explanation: Ground speed = v_plane cos 30° = 40 × (√3/2) = 20√3 ≈ 34.64 m/s.

medium.question: A man walking at 4 km/h notices that rain strikes him at an angle of 30° with the vertical. When he increases his speed to 8 km/h, the rain appears to strike him at an angle of 60° with the vertical. What is the vertical speed of the rain?

A river is flowing from West to East at 5 m/s. A swimmer on the South bank wants to reach a point directly opposite on the North bank. If his swimming speed in still water is 10 m/s, his heading angle with the direction of river flow should be:
medium.explanation: To cancel the eastward current of 5 m/s, the upstream component must be 10 cos(α) = 5 (where α is angle with upstream West) ⟹ cos α = 0.5 ⟹ α = 60° upstream from North, which is 90° + 30° = 120° from downstream flow direction East.

medium.question: Regarding a river-boat scenario where river current speed u exceeds boat speed v (i.e. u > v):

options.label: The boat can never reach the point directly opposite the starting point
The minimum drift is non-zero and positive
Drift is minimized when the upstream heading angle satisfies sin θ = v / u
The boat cannot cross to the other bank at all

medium.explanation: Because u > v, no heading can make ground velocity purely perpendicular (zero drift impossible, A and B true). By setting d(drift)/dθ = 0, minimum drift occurs at sin θ = v/u (C true). The boat can always cross as long as it has a non-zero velocity component across the river (D is false).

medium.question: A flag is mounted on a car moving East with velocity v_c. The wind is blowing North with velocity v_w. Which of the following statements are correct?

options.label: The flutter direction of the flag is along the relative velocity of wind with respect to the car
The flag flutters in the direction North-West
The angle of flutter with West is arctan(v_w / v_c)
The flag always points directly in the direction the wind is blowing relative to ground

medium.explanation: A flag flutters in the direction of air stream relative to the vehicle: v_w/c = v_w - v_c = v_w ĵ - v_c î (North-West direction). The angle with West (-î axis) is arctan(v_w / v_c).

medium.question: For two vectors A and B with angle θ between them:

options.label: If |A + B| = |A - B|, then A and B are orthogonal

medium.explanation: All four are fundamental vector identities. |A + B|² = A² + B² + 2AB cos θ, |A - B|² = A² + B² - 2AB cos θ. Adding them yields 2(A² + B²). Equating them gives 4AB cos θ = 0 ⟹ θ = 90°.

medium.question: A swimmer crosses a river of width W flowing at speed v_r. Swimmer speed in water is v_s.

options.label: If steered directly across, the crossing time is W / v_s
If steered directly across, the drift is W * v_r / v_s
If steered at angle θ upstream (sin θ = v_r / v_s), crossing time is W / (v_s cos θ)
Zero drift crossing time is always less than minimum crossing time

medium.explanation: Zero drift crossing time is W / (v_s cos θ) > W / v_s (since cos θ < 1), so zero drift time is always greater than minimum crossing time (D is false).

medium.question: Rain falls vertically at speed v. A person walks with speed u. Which of the following statements about relative rain motion are TRUE?

options.label: The apparent speed is sqrt(u^2 + v^2)
The umbrella must be held tilted forward at angle θ = arctan(u/v) to the vertical
If the person doubles their speed to 2u, the apparent speed becomes sqrt(4u^2 + v^2)
If wind starts blowing horizontally in the direction of the person's motion with speed u, rain appears vertical to the person

medium.explanation: v_r/m = (v_wind - u)î - v ĵ. If v_wind = u, then relative horizontal component is u - u = 0, so rain appears purely vertical. All four statements are correct.

medium.question: A plane has an airspeed of 500 km/h. A wind is blowing due West at 300 km/h. To fly due North, at what angle East of North (in degrees, to 1 decimal place) must the plane steer?
medium.explanation: To cancel the westward wind of 300 km/h, the plane must have an eastward component of 300 km/h: 500 sin θ = 300 ⟹ sin θ = 300/500 = 0.6 ⟹ θ = arcsin(0.6) ≈ 36.87° ≈ 36.9° East of North.

medium.question: In the question above (airspeed 500 km/h, wind 300 km/h West, heading due North), what is the resulting ground speed of the aircraft (in km/h)?
Rain is falling vertically at 12 m/s. A car travels horizontally at 16 m/s. What is the apparent speed of the rain as observed by the driver (in m/s)?
A boat can travel at 13 m/s in still water. It crosses a 240 m wide river flowing at 5 m/s along the shortest path (0 drift). How many seconds does the trip take?
medium.explanation: Effective cross-river speed = √(13² - 5²) = √(169 - 25) = √144 = 12 m/s. Crossing time = 240 / 12 = 20 seconds.

medium.question: A man can swim in still water at 4 m/s. He swims across a 120 m river with current 3 m/s in minimum time. What is his total ground displacement (in meters) upon reaching the opposite bank?
medium.explanation: Minimum time = 120 / 4 = 30 s. Drift = 3 × 30 = 90 m. Total displacement = √(120² + 90²) = √(14400 + 8100) = √22500 = 150 meters.

advanced.question: A particle is projected from the origin with initial velocity u at angle θ to the horizontal. At time t = (u sin θ) / g, its position vector r and velocity vector v are perpendicular. What must be the launch angle θ?
advanced.explanation: Position r = (u cos θ · t)î + (u sin θ · t - ½gt²)ĵ. Velocity v = (u cos θ)î + (u sin θ - gt)ĵ. For r • v = 0: u² cos²θ · t + (u sin θ · t - ½gt²)(u sin θ - gt) = 0. Substituting t = u sin θ / g: u² cos²θ · (u sin θ / g) + (u² sin²θ / g - ½ u² sin²θ / g)(0) = 0 ⟹ u³ cos²θ sin θ / g + (½ u² sin²θ / g)(-u² sin²θ / ...). In general, r • v = 0 gives t = (2u / g) · [sin θ / (1 + 2 cot²θ)]. Equating to u sin θ / g gives 2 / (1 + 2 cot²θ) = 1 ⟹ 1 + 2 cot²θ = 2 ⟹ cot²θ = 1/2 ⟹ tan²θ = 2 ⟹ sin²θ = 2/3 ⟹ sin θ = √(2/3) or for this condition sin θ = 1/√3.

advanced.question: A river of width W flows with variable velocity profile v_r(y) = 4 v_0 (y / W) (1 - y / W), where y is distance from one bank. A boat crosses maintaining constant velocity v_0 perpendicular to the current. What is the total downstream drift upon reaching y = W?
advanced.explanation: dy/dt = v_0 ⟹ dt = dy / v_0. Total drift x = ∫ v_r(y) dt = ∫[0 to W] [4 v_0 (y/W)(1 - y/W)] (dy / v_0) = (4/W) ∫[0 to W] (y - y²/W) dy = (4/W) [W²/2 - W³/3W] = (4/W) [W²/6] = 4/6 W = 2/3 W.

advanced.question: Two motorboats A and B start simultaneously from the same point on a wide lake. Boat A travels North at 30 km/h, and Boat B travels at 40 km/h in a direction 60° East of North. What is the speed of Boat B relative to Boat A?

A swimmer can swim with speed v relative to water. A river of width W flows with speed u (where u > v). The swimmer wants to cross the river with MINIMUM drift. What is the angle θ upstream from the perpendicular that minimizes drift?
advanced.explanation: Drift x(θ) = (u - v sin θ) * (W / (v cos θ)) = (W/v) * (u sec θ - v tan θ). Differentiating with respect to θ and setting to 0: u sec θ tan θ - v sec²θ = 0 ⟹ u tan θ = v sec θ ⟹ u (sin θ / cos θ) = v (1 / cos θ) ⟹ sin θ = v / u.

advanced.question: A ship steams due West at 15 knots. Another ship 10 nautical miles due South steams due North at 20 knots. What is the closest distance of approach between the two ships?
advanced.explanation: Let ship A be at origin moving West: v_A = -15î. Ship B is at -10ĵ moving North: v_B = 20ĵ. Relative velocity of B with respect to A: v_B/A = v_B - v_A = 15î + 20ĵ. Magnitude |v_B/A| = √(15² + 20²) = 25 knots. Initial separation r0 = -10ĵ. Closest distance d_min = |r0 × v_rel| / |v_rel| = |(-10ĵ) × (15î + 20ĵ)| / 25 = |150 k| / 25 = 6.0 nautical miles.

advanced.question: Two particles A and B are projected simultaneously from the same point with the same speed u at complementary elevation angles α and (90° - α). Which of the following statements are TRUE?

options.label: Both particles achieve the exact same horizontal range
The relative acceleration between the particles during flight is zero
The relative velocity between them remains constant in magnitude and direction
The line joining the two particles rotates at a constant angular velocity

advanced.explanation: Complementary angles give identical ranges: R = u² sin(2α)/g. Both experience acceleration -g ĵ, so relative acceleration a_rel = -g - (-g) = 0. Therefore, relative velocity v_rel is constant over time (B and C true). Since relative velocity is constant and they start from the same point, relative position is r_rel = v_rel · t, which is a straight line without rotation.

advanced.question: A vector field or navigation path in 2D relative motion satisfies r_rel(t) = r_0 + v_rel * t. Which of the following mathematical properties are valid?

options.label: Time of closest approach is t_min = -(r_0 • v_rel) / |v_rel|^2
Distance of closest approach is |r_0 × v_rel| / |v_rel|
At the moment of closest approach, r_rel(t_min) • v_rel = 0
If r_0 • v_rel > 0, the distance between them is strictly increasing for all t > 0

advanced.explanation: Let d²(t) = |r_0 + v_rel · t|² = r_0² + 2(r_0 • v_rel)t + v_rel² t². Differentiating: d/dt(d²) = 2(r_0 • v_rel) + 2 v_rel² t = 0 ⟹ t_min = -(r_0 • v_rel) / v_rel². At minimum, position is perpendicular to relative velocity (C true). The cross-product gives perpendicular distance (B true). If r_0 • v_rel > 0, the derivative is positive for all t > 0, so separation increases monotonically (D true).

advanced.question: A swimmer wishes to cross a river flowing with velocity v_r. Which of the following conditions lead to the minimum travel time or minimum distance?

options.label: Minimum crossing time is achieved strictly when heading angle θ = 0° perpendicular to the banks
If v_s > v_r, minimum distance path is perpendicular to the banks with zero drift
If v_r > v_s, minimum drift occurs at upstream angle sin θ = v_s / v_r
The path of minimum time is identical to the path of minimum distance for any flow rate

advanced.explanation: Minimum time requires maximizing the cross-river component (θ = 0°), which produces drift. Minimum distance requires canceling current (or minimizing drift when v_r > v_s). Thus the two paths are distinct whenever v_r > 0 (D is false).

advanced.question: A gun fires a shell from a train moving with velocity v_t î. The muzzle velocity relative to the gun is u at an elevation angle α in the forward vertical plane. Which statements are correct?

options.label: The horizontal velocity of the shell relative to ground is v_t + u cos α
The vertical velocity of the shell relative to ground is u sin α
The time of flight is independent of train speed v_t
The maximum height above launch level is independent of train speed v_t

advanced.explanation: Train motion is purely horizontal. The vertical motion is governed strictly by u_y = u sin α and gravity g. Thus time of flight T = 2u_y/g and max height H = u_y²/(2g) are completely independent of train speed v_t. Horizontal velocity relative to ground is v_t + u cos α.

advanced.question: Three identical particles A, B, C start at the vertices of an equilateral triangle of side a. Each moves at constant speed v directly towards the next (A towards B, B towards C, C towards A). Which of the following are TRUE?

options.label: The particles meet at the centroid of the triangle
The rate of approach between any pair is 1.5 v
The time taken to meet is 2a / (3v)
Total distance traveled by each particle is 2a / 3

advanced.explanation: By symmetry they spiral into the centroid. The relative velocity of approach along side AB is v - (-v cos 60°) = v + 0.5v = 1.5v = 3v/2. Time to meet t = a / (3v/2) = 2a / (3v). Distance traveled by each particle is v × t = v × (2a / 3v) = 2a / 3.

advanced.question: A river 600 m wide flows at 5 m/s. A boat travels at 3 m/s in still water. What is the minimum possible downstream drift (in meters) the boat can achieve while crossing?
advanced.explanation: Since vr (5) > vb (3), minimum drift occurs at sin θ = vb / vr = 3/5. Minimum drift = Width × √(vr² - vb²) / vb = 600 × √(25 - 9) / 3 = 600 × (4 / 3) = 800 meters.

advanced.question: A ship A moves North at 20 km/h. Ship B is initially 10 km East of A and moves West at 20 km/h. After how many minutes (to 1 decimal place) will they reach their closest point of approach?
advanced.explanation: Relative velocity v_B/A = -20î - 20ĵ. Magnitude |v_rel| = √(20² + 20²) = 20√2 km/h. Initial position r0 = 10î. Time of closest approach t = -(r0 • v_rel) / |v_rel|² = -(10 × (-20)) / (20√2)² = 200 / 800 = 0.25 hours = 15 minutes.

advanced.question: A projectile is launched from ground with speed 20 m/s at an angle of 30° above horizontal. Taking g = 10 m/s², what is the radius of curvature (in meters, to 1 decimal place) of its trajectory at the highest point?
advanced.explanation: At highest point, velocity is purely horizontal: v_top = u cos 30° = 20 × (√3/2) = 10√3 m/s. Centripetal acceleration is normal gravity: a_n = g = 10 m/s². Radius of curvature ρ = v_top² / a_n = (10√3)² / 10 = 300 / 10 = 30 meters.

advanced.question: Four particles A, B, C, D are located at the corners of a square of side 100 m. Each particle pursues the next in clockwise order at a constant speed of 10 m/s. How many seconds will it take for them to collide at the center?
advanced.explanation: At any instant, velocity of B is perpendicular to side AB (angle 90°), so its velocity component along AB is 0. Rate of approach along side AB is v - 0 = 10 m/s. Time to meet t = d / v = 100 / 10 = 10 seconds.

advanced.question: A helicopter flying at altitude 180 m with horizontal speed 50 m/s releases a supply bundle. Taking g = 10 m/s², what is the horizontal distance (in meters) traveled by the bundle before touching the ground?
advanced.explanation: Time of fall t = √(2H / g) = √(2 × 180 / 10) = √36 = 6 seconds. Horizontal distance = u × t = 50 × 6 = 300 meters.
